newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Eight agents die in Bogota police station blast.
newsitem.headline: Eight agents die in Bogota police station blast.

text.p: At least eight policemen were killed on Tuesday and more than 10 others were injured in a powerful explosion just outside a police station on the southwest outskirts of Bogota, authorities said.

Metropolitan Police chief Teodoro Campo said the explosion occurred in the back of a truck that was being searched in the police station's parking lot on suspicion that it had been loaded with contraband goods.
"We have a total of eight dead and more than 10 wounded," Campo told reporters.
He said he could not rule out the possibility that explosives, probably dynamite, had been placed aboard the truck by leftist guerrillas or drug traffickers.

But Campo stopped short of saying the explosion was directed against the police, since the truck had been towed to the police station in the working-class district of Fontibon after being confiscated elsewhere.

National Police director Gen. Rosso Jose Serrano said victims of the blast included three crack police intelligence officers as well as ordinary patrolmen who were aiding in the search of the vehicle.
